items.title: Germans see little progress on cutting red tape
items.description: Most people and businesses in Germany say they've seen little change in bureaucracy despite Chancellor Friedrich Merz's government promises to reduce it.

items.title: Who is Viktor Orbán, Hungarian PM fighting to stay in power after 16 years?
items.description: Since 2010, Orbán has transformed Hungary into what the European Parliament has denounced as a "hybrid regime of electoral autocracy".

items.title: Iran war lands 'triple blow' to flood-ravaged Sri Lankans
items.description: The Iran war could not have come at a worse time for Sri Lanka, reeling from devastating floods and an economic crisis.

items.title: India news: Delhi looks to ban fossil fuel two-wheelers from 2028
items.description: India's capital is gearing up to ban non-electric two-wheelers as it looks to tackle chronic smog and high pollution. In other news, PM Modi is campaigning in West Bengal ahead of high-stake elections.

items.title: 'Every drop of water counts': Fear for the future of Argentina's glaciers
items.description: A controversial law to ease protections for the glaciers has passed, opening the doors for mining.

items.title: Djibouti's president wins unprecedented sixth term with 97.8% of vote
items.description: Ismail Omar Guelleh, 78, has extended his already 27-year rule in a poll boycotted by the main opposition candidates.

items.title: Ukrainian civilians abducted, tortured in Russian prisons
items.description: Russia has been holding thousands of Ukrainian civilians behind bars for years, in breach of international humanitarian law. Families have been fighting for their loved ones to be released, some for more than a decade.
